official.deadline_note: The ACIAR page states applications for the 2027 intake are now closed. DFAT's published dates for study commencing in 2027 list an opening date of 1 February 2026 (09:00 AEDT) and a closing date of 30 April 2026 (14:00 AEST) for nearly all participating countries; Palau's country window differs (30 March 2026 to 30 June 2026). ACIAR's factsheet states applications open 1 February to 30 April and that they open from February to April each year, so the next round is expected to follow the same window, but no date beyond the 2027-intake round is published yet.
official.application_cycle: 2027 intake round (applications 1 February - 30 April 2026); annual cycle, with applications opening 1 February to 30 April each year
official.status_note: ACIAR's page states 'Applications for the 2027 intake are now closed' and the OASIS portal news board lists 'ACIAR John Allwright Fellowships' among the 2027 intake schemes whose applications have closed. The separate John Allwright Fellowship - Philippines co-funded round is also closed.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The ACIAR page lists 'Full tuition fees' among the benefits that generally apply. The Australia Awards Scholarships Policy Handbook Table 1 describes Academic Fees as covering 'the course costs and all compulsory academic fees that apply to international students', plus a Student Services and Amenities Fee paid directly to the institution.
benefits: Return air travel - payment of a single return, economy class airfare to and from Australia, via the most direct route

Establishment allowance - a once only payment as a contribution towards accommodation expenses, textbooks, study materials (A$5,000 paid once on arrival, per the Australia Awards Scholarships Policy Handbook)

Contribution to Living Expenses (CLE) - a fortnightly contribution to basic living expenses paid at a rate determined by the department (A$99.26 per day from 1 January 2026, approximately A$36,230 per annum)
Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) for the duration of the award (for award holder only)
Fieldwork may be available for eligible research students for one return economy class airfare via the most direct route to their country of citizenship or within Australia
eligibility: You must not be a citizen of Australia, hold permanent residency in Australia or be applying for a visa to live in Australia permanently
You must be a citizen of the country in which you are working
You are currently employed on a permanent or long-term contract basis

You are a scientist or economist who is actively involved in an ACIAR research project or small research activity within the last 24 months at the time of applying; ACIAR may consider supporting researchers from 'advanced pipeline' projects
You hold qualifications, equivalent to at least an Australian Bachelor degree, in a discipline that is relevant to the proposed area of postgraduate study
You are endorsed by your current employer, ACIAR Project Leaders (Commissioned Organisations and Country Collaborators) and your primary supervisor
requirements: Your Research Proposal addresses how gender equity, social inclusion and climate change will be considered in your research approach and impact your intended outcomes, and demonstrates how your research contributes to addressing a development priority of your country

You have recently undertaken an English language testing program, i.e. IELTS, TOEFL, PTE, or are prepared to take the test on receipt of application outcome (the ACIAR factsheet specifies a test undertaken within the last 6 months)
Study must be a Masters by Research or PhD at a registered Australian institution; Masters by Coursework is not eligible under the JAF program
The study program must relate to your area of proposed research, and listed courses are found on the Commonwealth Register of Institutions and Courses for Overseas Students (CRICOS)
Your nominated primary supervisor must be affiliated with the same Australian institution at which you study
Awardees must obtain a Student visa (subclass 500) and satisfy Department of Home Affairs requirements, demonstrating genuine temporary stay intentions
documents: An identity document (passport must have an expiry date more than 6 months from the application date)
Certified copies of degree certificates and certified copies of academic transcripts

Australian Project Leader referee report and Collaborating Country Project Leader referee report (templates available), plus a Primary Supervisor endorsement letter (formal letter or copy of email correspondence)
selection_criteria: Alignment and relevancy to ACIAR Research projects
Potential for impact, including the applicants' intended plans upon returning home after completing their studies
Alignment of the proposal to the research and development priorities of the applicant's home country

Written endorsements outlined in supporting documents (current employer, Australian project leader, collaborating country project leader, and primary supervisor affiliated with the institution of study)
How well the proposal demonstrates the gender equity and social inclusion, climate change, as well as the project contribution to the development priority of your country
coverage: Full tuition fees, covering course costs and all compulsory academic fees that apply to international students, plus the Student Services and Amenities Fee
Return air travel - a single return, economy class airfare to and from Australia, via the most direct route (mobilisation and completion travel in the Australia Awards Scholarships Policy Handbook)
Establishment allowance - A$5,000 towards expenses such as rental bonds, textbooks, study materials, additional medical insurance and home contents insurance

Contribution to Living Expenses - a fortnightly contribution to basic living expenses, A$99.26 per day from 1 January 2026 (approximately A$36,230 per annum), covering accommodation, transport, food, entertainment and stationery
Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) for the duration of the award for the award holder, and payment of visa processing and medical checks necessary for the Student visa (subclass 500)

Introductory Academic Program (IAP), a compulsory 4-6 week program prior to formal academic studies; supplementary academic support of A$500 every six months on-scholarship; and reunion airfare for unaccompanied awardees whose scholarship period is two years or more
application_method: Register an account in the Online Australia Scholarships Information System (OASIS)
Log on, create and complete an OASIS application form
Select the ACIAR John Allwright Fellowships award program when starting an application
Upload the mandatory supporting documents with your application
Refer to the OASIS Applicant User Guide for instructions on registering and creating an application
Read the Australia Awards Scholarships Policy Handbook, which the JAF program is guided by, before signing the contract with the Commonwealth of Australia
official.application_route: Apply online through OASIS (oasis.dfat.gov.au): register an account, create an application, select the ACIAR John Allwright Fellowships award program, and upload the mandatory documents before the round closes; general enquiries go to capacity.building@aciar.gov.au.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must be citizens of an ACIAR participating partner country in Africa, South Asia, East and Southeast Asia or the Pacific, excluding India and Myanmar, and must be a citizen of the country in which they are working. ACIAR's country partnerships span the Pacific (Fiji, Kiribati, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, Vanuatu), East and Southeast Asia (Cambodia, China, Indonesia, Laos, Mongolia, Philippines, Thailand, Timor-Leste, Vietnam), South Asia (Bangladesh, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka) and Africa (Ethiopia, Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, Rwanda, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia, Zimbabwe). Applicants must not hold Australian citizenship or permanent residency or be seeking to live in Australia permanently.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the Fellowship is designed for non-Australian applicants from ACIAR partner countries. Applicants must not be Australian citizens or permanent residents, must not be applying for a visa to live in Australia permanently, and, under the Australia Awards Policy, must not be married to, engaged to or a de facto of an Australian or New Zealand citizen or permanent resident during application, selection and mobilisation.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Applicants must be scientists or economists actively involved in an ACIAR research project or small research activity within the last 24 months at the time of applying; ACIAR may consider supporting researchers from 'advanced pipeline' projects. The study program must relate to the applicant's area of proposed research. In the 2026 intake round ACIAR allocated places specifically for research dedicated to addressing climate change, climate adaptation or strengthening resilience to climate change impacts.
official.research_requirement: All Master and PhD applicants must submit a research proposal, written after discussions with their project leader, under mandated subheadings: proposed title; objectives; relationship of this research to previous work in this field by yourself or others; how it relates to the research you are presently undertaking in the ACIAR project; significance and possible application of the proposed research to your country's development priorities; and research methodology, including how your research considers the impacts of climate change, how you intend to translate your research findings into actions on conclusion of your program, whether any aspects address climate change adaptation or mitigation, how your research considers and addresses gender equity and social inequalities, and any fieldwork component.
official.duration: The JAF is offered for the minimum period necessary for the individual to complete the academic program specified by the Australian higher education institution, including any preparatory training. The Australia Awards Scholarships Policy Handbook specifies the Introductory Academic Program as 4-6 weeks and pre-course English language training for up to a maximum of six months.
official.description: The John Allwright Fellowship is a competitive, merit-based program available to scientists or economists from partner countries currently or recently involved in ACIAR research projects, offering the opportunity to obtain formal postgraduate qualifications at an Australian tertiary institution. Administered through the Australia Awards system, it is the largest investment in ACIAR's Capacity Development Program and aims to strengthen scientific research capability and institutional links in ACIAR partner countries to undertake high-quality and impactful research.
official.region: Study in Australia; open to applicants from ACIAR partner countries across Africa, South Asia, East and Southeast Asia and the Pacific
official.program_type: Australian Government scholarship - ACIAR postgraduate research scholarship administered through the Australia Awards system
official.english_requirement: Under the Australia Awards Scholarships Policy Handbook, all awardees must meet: Academic IELTS with an overall score of at least 6.5 with no band less than 6.0, OR an internet-based TOEFL score of at least 84 (or 90 on the new scale applying from 21 January 2026) with a minimum of 21 in all subtests, OR PTE Academic overall score of 58 with no communicative skill score less than 50. Scores are described as not negotiable, test results must be valid at 1 January of the year of commencing studies (IELTS, TOEFL and PTE Academic results are valid for two years), and where an institution's academic English language requirement is higher, the institution's requirement applies. The JAF application requirement is that you have recently undertaken an English language testing program, i.e. IELTS, TOEFL, PTE, or are prepared to take the test on receipt of application outcome, with the ACIAR factsheet specifying a test undertaken within the last 6 months. Pre-course English training of up to six months in-country or in Australia may be available for applicants within half an IELTS point of 6.5.

applicant_utility.summary: This is not an open-call scholarship you can apply to cold: entry depends on being a scientist or economist who is, or was within the last 24 months, actively involved in an ACIAR-funded research project, and on securing employer, project-leader and supervisor endorsements before the window opens. The award is genuinely full - full tuition, return airfares, a A$5,000 establishment allowance and a living contribution of A$99.26 per day - so the money is rarely the reason applicants fail. The binding constraint is documentary and relational: the round for study commencing in 2027 closed on 30 April 2026, so the practical job now is assembling an OASIS application and the four mandated endorsements ready for the next 1 February opening.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Mid-career agricultural researchers and economists already embedded in an ACIAR project who need a Master's by Research or PhD at an Australian institution, can secure employer and project-leader endorsements, and intend to return home to apply what they learn.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your ACIAR project involvement falls inside the 24-month window at the time you apply - work older than 24 months is disqualifying, and 'advanced pipeline' projects are only considered at ACIAR's discretion.

Brief and secure all four endorsements months in advance: current employer, Australian Project Leader, Collaborating Country Project Leader and your prospective primary supervisor, each on the template provided in OASIS.

Verify your intended course is a Master's by Research or PhD listed on CRICOS and that your proposed primary supervisor is affiliated with that same institution - a coursework Master's makes the application ineligible outright.

Sit IELTS Academic, TOEFL iBT or PTE Academic early: aim for overall 6.5 with no band under 6.0, keep the test inside the factsheet's 6-month window, and remember the score must still be valid at 1 January of your commencement year.

Have degree certificates and transcripts certified in line with Section 2.8 of the Australia Awards Scholarships Policy Handbook, and check your passport expires more than six months past your application date.

Draft the research proposal under the factsheet's mandated subheadings, explicitly covering climate change impacts, adaptation or mitigation, translation of findings into action, gender equity and social inequalities, and any fieldwork component, then have an expert reviewer read it before submission.
common_rejection_risks: Missing any of the four written endorsements - ACIAR states that failure to provide these documents directly impacts your eligibility.
Naming a Master's by Coursework program, which ACIAR states is not eligible under the JAF program.
Falling outside the 24-month ACIAR involvement window, or nominating a primary supervisor who is not affiliated with the institution you list.

A research proposal that does not visibly connect to a specific ACIAR project and to a stated development priority of your home country, or that omits the climate change and gender equity analysis the selection criteria explicitly weight.
An English test result older than six months, or below overall 6.5 / band 6.0, since the policy states scores are not negotiable and an institution's higher bar prevails.
Australian or New Zealand citizenship or permanent residency held by a spouse, partner or de facto, which breaches the scheme's eligibility rules during application, selection and mobilisation.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Awardees are responsible for all their expenses in Australia including those of any family members. Single Overseas Student Health Cover excludes pre-existing conditions and ancillary services such as dental, physiotherapy and optical care, which must be purchased at the awardee's own expense, as must additional medical insurance and travel insurance for travel outside Australia. Airfares to a third country that is not your home country are not covered unless tied to a DFAT-approved compulsory fieldwork trip. Bring your own funds to bridge the gap before the A$5,000 establishment allowance is paid and note the living contribution stops five days after thesis submission, release of results, or departure from Australia.
document_audit: Certification of degree certificates and transcripts is a common failure point - follow Section 2.8 of the Australia Awards Scholarships Policy Handbook on acceptable certified copies rather than assuming a scan suffices.
Your passport must expire more than six months after your application date, so renew before the round opens if it is close.

The employer endorsement letter, Australian Project Leader referee report and Collaborating Country Project Leader referee report each have mandatory templates in OASIS - use them rather than free-form letters.
The primary supervisor endorsement may be a formal letter or a copy of email correspondence, so written confirmation of their willingness must exist before you submit.
The research proposal must sit under the factsheet's prescribed subheadings; a free-form essay that omits the climate, gender equity and fieldwork sections will be scored down.
Highly recommended extras that strengthen the file but are not mandatory: current CV, list of publications, and a university statement that English is the language of instruction.
alerts: Applications for the 2027 intake are already closed; the practical deadline to plan against is the next round's 1 February opening and 30 April close, with the window historically running 09:00 AEDT on the opening day to 14:00 AEST on the closing day.

Awardees must leave Australia for a minimum of two years after completing the scholarship, and failure to do so incurs a debt for the total accrued cost - plan your career on that basis before accepting.
An offer is only valid for the Australian academic year following the calendar year in which the offer is made, so a deferred place is not automatically carried forward.

Visa applications can take up to three months, and the Department of Home Affairs requires genuine temporary stay intentions - apply for your Student visa (subclass 500) immediately after signing the contract.
Involvement in an ACIAR project that ended more than 24 months ago makes you ineligible for this round, so check your project dates before investing effort in the proposal.
Applicants with dual citizenship should apply for their visa using the passport of the country for which they received the Fellowship.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register in OASIS, complete the application form selecting the ACIAR John Allwright Fellowships award program, upload the mandatory documents, and submit before the round closes; ACIAR then weights the research proposal and endorsements, places successful applicants with an Australian institution, and issues the scholarship contract for signature.
